probe.reason: clang cannot build wasm32 here (it needs the WebAssembly target and wasm-ld)

headers.math.h:
/* freestanding math for wasm32 (platform/wasm card): WebAssembly instructions only */
#define sqrt(x) __builtin_sqrt(x)
#define fabs(x) __builtin_fabs(x)
#define floor(x) __builtin_floor(x)
#define ceil(x) __builtin_ceil(x)
#define trunc(x) __builtin_trunc(x)
#define nearbyint(x) __builtin_nearbyint(x)
#define copysign(x, y) __builtin_copysign(x, y)
#define fmin(x, y) __builtin_fmin(x, y)
#define fmax(x, y) __builtin_fmax(x, y)
#define INFINITY __builtin_inf()
#define NAN __builtin_nan("")
#define isnan(x) __builtin_isnan(x)
#define isinf(x) __builtin_isinf(x)
#define signbit(x) __builtin_signbit(x)

embed.statement: compile the C module to wasm32, inline it (base64) before the JavaScript request server; the server's transport (Node, or a hosting platform's such as the browser's) runs it

honest_limits: No libc: a machine module that calls a libm function other than the WebAssembly instructions does not build. Memory is the module's static data; machine modules allocate nothing.
name: wasm
statement: WebAssembly. The C language card's machine module compiled for wasm32 (clang, no libc) and served by the JavaScript request server, so it runs wherever JavaScript runs: Node, and any browser (engine wasm@browser). Integers are the C card's int64, the same words as the native library.
